evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.4.68: operam, cūram, pecūniam impendant in eās rēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With in and the accusative of what the money goes on. The cost itself is impēnsa or sūmptus.

evidence: Gell. 2.24.11: sēstertiōs trīcēnōs in cēnam (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 6.2.4: omnīnō nūllus in imperiō meō sūmptus factus est
Cic. Fam. 12.30.4: sūmptum in rem mīlitārem facere (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: illud, mī Tīrō, tē rogō, sūmptū nē parcās ūllā in rē, quod ad valētūdinem opus sit
phrases.english: this I beg of you, my dear Tiro: don’t spare expense on anything your health needs

phrases.latin: praestābō sūmptum nusquam melius posse pōnī
phrases.english: I promise you the money could not be better spent anywhere
How much did you spend on the shoes?
